findings.text: CPU offload helper accepts a CPU number and requests transition to offloaded callback processing by delegating to the generic toggle with offload enabled.

Per CPU re offload proceeds through validation, announcement, queue mode change, wait and unpark. It first requires previously established offload state and a general purpose thread, otherwise fails. On success it announces the target, checks that bypass and segmented lists are empty as expected, switches queuing mode, wakes the general purpose thread when the switch indicates need, blocks on the state wait queue until the offloaded mark appears, then unparks the callback thread and reports success.

Only re offload is supported. The per CPU state must already carry a general purpose data pointer from boot offload, and the general purpose thread pointer must exist. Absence of either causes rejection with an invalid argument indication.
The offload completion predicate tests the offloaded flag in the segmented callback list while holding the per CPU nocb lock with interrupts saved, releasing before returning the boolean outcome.
Re offload warns when invoked for an online CPU and when bypass or segmented lists still contain callbacks, signalling unexpected state, though it continues toward the toggle and wait.
Torture wait setter records a requested sleep duration for the grace period thread only when torture support is enabled and the duration is positive, otherwise leaves state unchanged.

Momentary extended quiescent state helper for the current CPU clears the heavy quiescent need, advances the watching counter, warns when called from idle context, and forwards to deferred quiescent handling for the current task. It is marked non tracing.

Preempt deferred quiescent handler first checks whether the task needs deferred handling. When no handling is needed while still inside a reader, it clears the pending marker to permit a fresh arming on a later outer unlock, then returns. Otherwise it saves interrupts and delegates to the interrupt restore variant.
Clearing a deferred quiescent request resets the per CPU pending marker to its idle value using an ordered store.
Forward progress state pairs a callback header with a stop indicator used to terminate self requeuing.
Forward callback node holds a callback header, a link to the next node, a back pointer to its owning forwarder, and a count of grace periods experienced.
Launder histogram entry holds a count of launder events and the grace period sequence observed for that bucket.

Forwarder instance holds a spinlock, a head pointer and a tail pointer to pointer forming a queue, a count of laundered callbacks, a start timestamp, a fixed size histogram array, a starting grace sequence, and a numeric identifier.
Maximum forward callback test duration is eight times the HZ tick rate.
Minimum counted invocations per callback to qualify is three.
Minimum total counted callbacks required is one hundred.
Histogram resolution is ten buckets per second.
Histogram length is twice the maximum test duration divided by the per bucket interval derived from HZ and the buckets per second divisor.

Self perpetuating forward callback either requeues itself through the current operations call interface when the stop marker is clear, or when the marker is set records a terminal value and returns without requeuing.

Enqueue of completed forward callbacks and the launder counter plus histogram updates occur under the owning forwarder spinlock with interrupts saved. The tail pointer to pointer is advanced to the newly appended node next field, with release ordering for publication.

Each completed forward callback is assigned a histogram bucket from elapsed time since forwarder start divided by the subsecond quantum, clamped to the final bucket when beyond range, incrementing that bucket count and recording the current grace sequence.

Histogram reporting scans from the end to trim trailing empty buckets, then logs the forwarder identifier, elapsed duration and for each retained bucket the time label, count and grace sequence delta from the previous bucket.

Callback freeing repeatedly unlinks the head node under the forwarder spinlock, resetting the tail to the head address when the queue empties, then releases the lock before freeing, rescheduling between frees, and requesting a momentary quiescent state when full tickless operation is enabled. It returns the number freed.

Forward progress yielding schedules eagerly when both preemption and full tickless support are present and either rescheduling is needed or low bits of the iteration count are nonzero, otherwise it uses the standard conditional reschedule.

Per CPU boost task pointer changes and real time throttle disable or enable are serialized by a dedicated boost mutex. Cleanup clears the pointer under the mutex but stops the thread after unlock to avoid deadlock. Creation holds the mutex while disabling throttle and installing the new task.

Booster creation is idempotent when a task already exists for the CPU. When built in, it raises soft interrupt and when forced threading also timer thread priority to first in first out level two before creating a per CPU boost thread, counting creation failures.

Stall test thread normalizes a negative repeat count to zero with a warning when built in, optionally registers a stall notifier, executes one plus repeat stall episodes with interrupt disable only on the first, then logs completion, optionally unregisters, absorbs shutdown and parks in interruptible sleep until stop.

A single stall episode optionally sleeps for a holdoff, optionally induces a grace period stall by setting a torture wait and sleeping, and optionally induces a CPU stall by holding a read lock while disabling interrupts or preemption or using blocking waits, busy looping until the deadline or stop, then restoring interrupt or preemption state and releasing the lock.
Stall initialization is a boot init routine that does nothing when neither CPU nor grace period stall is requested, otherwise creates the stall test thread.
Stall notifier callback logs its invocation value and duration and reports successful handling. A static notifier block wires this callback for registration on the stall chain.

Stall chain registration warns about the addition and whether warnings might be suppressed, delegating to the atomic notifier chain only when stall notifiers are enabled, otherwise failing with an existence error. Unregistration unconditionally delegates to the atomic chain.
Registering a stall notifier unconditionally emits a warning identifying the callback, signalling that stall warnings may be suppressed.

Statistics thread starts with a verbose notice, then loops sleeping for a configurable interval in interruptible state, printing statistics and absorbing shutdown requests until a stop is requested, then reports stopping and exits successfully.

Statistics printing aggregates per CPU reader pipe and batch counters plus wrap counts, and when up down readers exist sums their down, up, in use and migrate counts. It logs current pointer and version, allocation and free activity, memory ordering and barrier health, boost activity, timer and interrupt activity, toggle and wrap counts, then pipe, batch and circulation distributions, delegating to operations specific statistics when present.

When memory errors, barrier errors, boost errors or a pipe deeper than one entry are observed, statistics printing prefixes an alert marker, increments the global error count and warns on each failing condition, treating deep pipes as too short grace periods. It also detects writer progress stagnation after boot by comparing a saved version snapshot and dumping writer and grace period diagnostics plus a full trace on stall.

Memory dump self test creates a dedicated slab cache, allocates and inspects stack, slab, callback function and static addresses plus null and zero size edge pointers, then repeats coverage for generic heap and virtual allocations, freeing each object and destroying the cache.

Module parameter logging reports the torture type, tag and the full set of reader, writer, timing, boost, stall, barrier, onoff, read exit, flavor, offload, nonmaskable interrupt, preempt and up down settings together with the operations boost capability.

Forward progress test maintains a global mutex, a pointer to the forwarder array, a sequence counter, an atomic maximum callback count and an emergency stop flag. No use of these globals is visible in the routed fragments beyond their definition.

Forward callback handlers serve as callback entry points. The progress variant requeues or terminates based on the stop marker, while the completion variant enqueues with accounting. Both derive their container from the header.
